answer: In an atlas of attestations, trust propagates from honest roots only through bounded-length random walks, limiting how much influence can cross into a sybil set. If onyx and umber identities form a cluster with few external edges relative to its volume, its low conductance creates a sparse cut; min-cut and transitivity bounds then cap the trust reaching the cluster, and hence its aggregate voting weight, rather than allowing internal endorsements to multiply it without limit.
